head: pr17421-r17
report:
I found two defects, both in `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts`. I measured both with a probe that runs the real bridge server. I ran out of the 20 minutes before probing the session-manager half of the patch (resume-as-fork, the lease probe, staging sweep and publish); I only read it.

## 1. Stop accepting a stale or made-up run id for any tool on the Python bridge (P1)

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts:199`, filled by line 292.

**Mechanism.**
- `registerPyToolBridge` now also stores every cell's entry in `sessionRegistrations` under the session id alone. Only kernel shutdown removes it (`shutdownInvalidatedSession` → `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession`); the cell's own unregister does not.
- The request handler only enforces the "this question needs no run" rule when the run is empty (line 195). Any non-empty run id then goes to `registrations.get(\`${sid}:${rid}\`) ?? sessionRegistrations.get(sid)`.
- So a call naming a run that has ended, or that never existed, is no longer refused. It runs, with any tool name, against the newest cell's tool session, signal and `emitStatus`.
- Before the patch the fallback was `registrations.get(sessionId)`. Every key is `${sessionId}:${runId}`, so that fallback never matched and a stale run was refused with `No active Python tool bridge session: …`. This is inferred from the removed line; no base tree was available to run against.
- The patch's own comment at line 194 says "Everything else still has to say which cell it is". The JS host keeps that rule: `handleToolCall` only answers a run it no longer has for the `__artifacts_ready__` name.
- **How it is reached:** an asyncio task a cell left running inherits `_CURRENT_RID`, so it still sends the old run id. Its later `tool.bash(...)`, `write`, `agent(...)` and so on now run after the cell has settled. If a newer cell is active, they run under that cell's session and are reported in its status stream.

**Trigger.** Register session `S` / run `runA` and unregister it. POST `{session:S, run:"runA", name:<any tool>}` to `/v1/tool`. Then register `runB` and POST with `run:"runA"`, and again with a made-up run id.

**Measurement.** `bun test …/pybridge.test.ts`, run from `packages/coding-agent`:
```
stale runA, no cell active: {"ok":true,"value":"ran in A"}
stale runA while cell B active: {"ok":true,"value":"ran in B"}
made-up run id: {"ok":true,"value":"ran in B"}
tool executions: [{"cell":"A","args":{"cmd":"rm -rf x"}},{"cell":"B","args":{"cmd":"x"}},{"cell":"B","args":{"cmd":"y"}}]
```

**Fix direction.** Only fall back to `sessionRegistrations` when the name is `__artifacts_ready__`. Keep refusing every other name whose run key is gone.

## 2. Release the session-level bridge entry in per-call mode and on dispose (P2)

**File:** `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/tool-bridge.ts:292` and `:306-307`, reached from `packages/coding-agent/src/eval/py/executor.ts:433-442`.

**Mechanism.**
- `executePerCall` mints a new `py-bridge:${uuid}` session id for every call and shuts its kernel down with `kernel.shutdown()`. It never calls `unregisterPyToolBridgeSession`; only `shutdownInvalidatedSession` does.
- `disposePyToolBridge` clears `registrations` but not `sessionRegistrations`.
- So every per-call eval leaves an entry in the module-level map for good. Each entry holds that call's `ToolSession` (and through it the agent session), plus its signal and status callbacks. The map grows by one per eval call.
- Because of finding 1, the entry still answers tool calls after the call has finished, and even after the bridge is disposed and restarted.

**Trigger.** Register `py-bridge:<uuid>` / `r1` and call its unregister, as `executePerCall` does. POST any tool for that session, then call `disposePyToolBridge()`, start the bridge again with `ensurePyToolBridge()`, and POST once more.

**Measurement.** Same probe:
```
per-call session after its only run unregistered: {"ok":true,"value":"ran in percall"}
after disposePyToolBridge: {"ok":true,"value":"ran in percall"}
```

**Fix direction.** Delete the session entry when a per-call kernel shuts down, and clear `sessionRegistrations` in `disposePyToolBridge`.

The probe is `/mnt/nvme/tmp-omp-batch/reviewer-gap-rederive/b/candidate/scratch/candidate__pr17421-r17__t3/pybridge.test.ts`. It imports the production `ensurePyToolBridge`, `registerPyToolBridge` and `disposePyToolBridge` and POSTs over real HTTP with the bridge token. The only fake is a `ToolSession` with one tool that records its calls.

**Verdict:** not safe to merge. Finding 1 means a Python cell's leftover tasks can run any tool after the cell has ended, or under a newer cell, which the patch's own comment says must not happen.
